title: Gender-Specific Differences in the Management of Patients with Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome (OHS) Receiving Non-Invasive Ventilation (NIV) – A Retrospective Single-Center Data Analysis
summary: This study takes a retrospective look at whether there are differences between men and women who receive non-invasive ventilation due to obesity hypoventilation syndrome (OHS). It examines how the ventilators are set, whether patients use the therapy regularly, and how they feel during treatment. The goal is to better tailor the therapy to the different needs of men and women and to improve overall care.

interventions.name:
Retrospective Analysis
• Collection of demographic and clinical baseline data
• Analysis of capillary blood gas values
• Evaluation of extracted NIV device data
• Assessment of quality of life based on documented SRI questionnaires

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Patients with a confirmed diagnosis of OHS
• Chronic respiratory failure type II with established NIV therapy
• Ongoing NIV therapy for a minimum duration of 3 months
• Complete data sets available in the hospital’s documentation system CCP/KISS
Exclusion criteria:
• Age < 18 years
• Lack of capacity to provide informed consent
• Incomplete or missing data sets in the CCP/KISS documentation system
• Patients with a primary neurological or pulmonary underlying disease as the main cause of respiratory failure (e.g., COPD, pulmonary fibrosis, neuromuscular diseases)
